valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 14 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one segment in effect, integrated Sri Lankan telecom (mobile 78% of nine-month 2026 revenue, broadband 15%, TV 7%), so one sector beta. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets unlevered beta for telecom (betaEmerg, January 2026) could NOT be read: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. As a stand-in, his US Telecom Services unlevered beta (January 2026, cash-corrected 0.38, from a web-search extract of his Betas page) was used; recheck with the emerging-markets figure. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 56.7bn ÷ market value Rs 461.9bn = 0.12 and 22.2% tax: 0.38 × (1 + 0.778 × 0.12) = 0.42. (4) Local 5-year betas from web-search extracts (the pages themselves couldn't be opened): StockAnalysis 0.66 (5Y), Investing.com 0.48 (5Y), Simply Wall St 0.63 (period not stated); median 0.63. Not a thinly traded share. (5) Higher of 0.42 and 0.63 = 0.63. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset and three verified local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (14 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.63 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 14.7%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 18 / 16.5 / 15%.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 2% then 3.5% / Base 5% then 4.5% / Bull 7% then 5.5%
valuationInputs.reason: Lowered a point (was 3/6/8% then 4/5/6%) because 2025 reinvestment supports little growth; long-run below the 12.24% bond and WACC, reinvesting growth ÷ return on capital (23% / 23% / 22%).

valuationInputs.name: ROE path
valuationInputs.reason: Unchanged; discounted at the new cost of equity.

valuationInputs.name: 2027 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: Forward P/E justified at the new cost of equity: payout (1 − g ÷ ROE, long-run ROE 20/25/30%, g 3.5/4.5/5.5%) ÷ (r − g). Base EPS = run-rate Rs 4.00 (Q3 2026 × 4).

valuationInputs.name: Dividend per share, growth
valuationInputs.reason: Growth lowered with the growth input; above the −1.4% capex-based supported rate for the reasons in the Growth check, below the 7.8% equity-route rate. Cash after maintenance covers dividends 1.08x (2025) to 1.4x (12 months to Sep 2026).

valuationInputs.name: Margins of safety
valuationInputs.reason: Medium confidence (methods Rs 27–32 in the base case; beta provisional).

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 24bn / Base Rs 36bn / Bull Rs 42bn
valuationInputs.reason: Cash before interest. Bear = calculator FY 2025 (operating cash 65.53 + after-tax interest 6.67 − depreciation 48.16). Base = 12 months to Sep 2026 (81.97 + 4.85 − base maintenance 46.30 = 40.5) less about 4.5 for capex payables still to be paid. Bull ≈ calculator FY 2025 at bull maintenance (40.3) and the trailing figure.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Bear = depreciation as reported; base = less impairment (1.00) and licence amortisation (0.86); bull = average capex booked 2024–2025. Depreciation includes Rs 7.6bn of contract-cost amortisation (cash already in operating cash flow) and Rs 2.8bn of lease depreciation, so bear and base are conservative.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: Unchanged. 2025 return on capital 18.2% (after-tax operating profit ÷ opening equity and net debt); about 26% on trailing profit and September capital.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 32bn / Base Rs 39bn / Bull Rs 42bn
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing operating profit Rs 50.3bn taxed at 22% (base, the 2025 rate); bear at 30% with some fade, for the risk that the BOI revenue-tax deal ends (goodwill note, AR 2025 p. 241); bull 16%, near the 2026 rate. Was Rs 36 / 40 / 44bn worked out from net profit.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 2% / 5% / 7%; supported -1.4% (reinvestment rate × return on capital, FY 2025). Bear 3.4, base 6.4, bull 8.4 pts above: kept because 2025 reinvestment was depressed by a one-off Rs 16.6bn pay-down of payables and a capex dip; 2026 capex booked (Rs 35.0bn in nine months) is back at depreciation with 5G spectrum bought and Rs 15.7bn contracted; revenue is growing 8% on the existing network; and the DCF charges growth ÷ return on capital in reinvestment every year. Equity route (profit kept × ROE) 7.8%.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2025 figures recorded in this redo; assumptions lowered a point from 3 / 6 / 8%.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (14 Nov 2026): cost of debt 8.25% (interest paid ÷ average borrowings and leases, 2025), tax 22.2%, debt weight 10.9% (net debt Rs 56.7bn, market cap Rs 461.9bn at Rs 50.20).

openQuestions: Beta: replace the provisional 0.63 in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets telecom unlevered beta (betaEmerg) and three verified local 5-year betas; this run couldn't open those sites.

Full-year 2026 results (due early February 2027): final dividend, capex booked vs paid (Rs 35.0bn vs Rs 19.0bn in nine months), working-capital swing, and whether 2026 reinvestment turns positive (capex above depreciation).
BOI tax concession: the 2025 goodwill note mentions an 'impending expiration of tax concession in year 2027' (p. 241). Does the 2% revenue-based tax end, and what rate applies after?
Does Dialog give any maintenance/growth capex split for 5G and fibre?
Why did the asset-retirement provision rise by about Rs 4bn in January–March 2026? Look in the 2026 annual report's provisions note.
Nine-month 2026 dividends paid Rs 33.5bn (cash flow) vs Rs 26.7bn (company equity statement): what is the difference?
Effect of deconsolidating Digital Health (now an associate) in Q4 2026; any 2027 budget changes to telecom levies.

changeLog.basedOn: H1 2026 reports plus Q3 2026 headline figures
changeLog.summary: Full re-research under the new framework: all five reports read with page references; added ratios, peers, macro, stress test, decision box. Cost of equity now a 18/16.5/15% range on a 12.4% bond; FCFE base Rs 43bn; ROE starts at 40%. Corrected the 2025 final dividend (Rs 1.50, not Rs 2.20). Category unchanged (watch list).

Read the full September 2026 interim report: it confirmed the press figures used this morning (Q3 profit Rs 9.24bn, EPS Rs 1.00). Q3 2025 profit set to the reported Rs 5.693bn (was 5.696 worked out). New September balance sheet: NAV Rs 9.99, borrowings Rs 64.1bn, net debt 0.58x EBITDA. Valuation inputs kept: trailing FCFE Rs 50.7bn is above the Rs 43bn base, but Rs 35bn of capex was booked in nine months against Rs 19bn paid, so not raised. Residual income rises with the higher book value (base Rs 23.0 → 23.7). Business tests 3 of 4; category unchanged (watch list).

P/E capped at the growth-justified 6 / 7.5 / 9.5x (was 8 / 10 / 12x): Rs 38.5 → 29.3. Dividend bull growth capped at 7.5%: Rs 25.0 → 26.2. Residual income unchanged (Rs 23.9). Growth check: assumed 3/6/8% vs 7.8% supported (profit kept × ROE), all within 2 pts; capex-based check not possible because FY 2025 depreciation, working capital and operating profit aren't in the record (set to null with notes). Warning: capex paid below depreciation in 2025 and 9M 2026. Business tests re-scored: 3 of 4, unchanged; category unchanged (watch list).
